subject: Trial hosting posture & onboarding checklist (next steps & owners)
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Maxwell <alice@beta.health>, Tom Hirsch <tom@beta.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-09-15T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Trial hosting posture & initial success criteria

Hi Alice / Tom —

Thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and a proposed short plan for the pilot so we can align on next steps: 

Key goals (what success looks like for Beta Health during the POC)
- Functional: REDWOOD returns structured extraction for clinical notes with precision >= 0.86 on your sample set (we'll use the 200-case seed you mentioned).
- Performance: 95th percentile end-to-end response latency < 350ms for single-request scenario and sustainable throughput of ~200 qps for batched inference windows.
- Security/compliance: Trial environment must support VPC peering or private-hosted option with customer-managed keys (KMS) and token-level audit logs.

Environment options we discussed (we'll recommend one after you confirm security constraints):
1) Hosted sandbox (fastest to start, no infra changes; not suitable for PHI).
2) Dedicated sandbox (isolated capacity on our managed infra; supports KMS and enhanced logging).
3) Customer VPC (private deployment into your VPC; best for PHI and strict network controls).

Proposed evaluation plan & timeline (2-week baseline trial):
- Week 0 (this week): Agreement on environment + sign DPA (procurement).
- Week 1: Environment provision and baseline dataset ingest; run smoke tests.
- Week 2: Closed-loop evaluation (quality metrics + latency/throughput tests); enable logging/trace collection and handover meeting.

Owners / points of contact
- Redwood: Sean Gallagher (trial lead), Marissa Cole (VPC/onboarding ops), Ben Carter (capacity/config).
- Beta Health: Alice Maxwell (product lead), Tom Hirsch (security).

Attachments: redwood-trial-mop.pdf (proposed minimal onboarding plan). Please send the SOC2/PII controls questionnaire if you have one — I flagged procurement on this thread.

Next actions for you: confirm preferred environment (Hosted / Dedicated / VPC) and available start date (earliest we could start provisioning is 2025-09-22). Also share any firewall/IP allowlist, KMS requirements, and the SOC2 questionnaire.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 15 min sync if easier.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Alice Maxwell <alice@beta.health>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Hirsch <tom@beta.health>, procurement <procurement@beta.health>
Date: 2025-09-16T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Trial hosting posture & initial success criteria

Sean —

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming a few items from our side and a couple of ask-abouts: 

Confirmed preferences / constraints:
- We need the trial to be hosted in our VPC due to PHI/data governance and MC/BC requirements.
- KMS must be customer-managed; BTW we use AWS KMS with key rotation policies.
- Audit logs at token/request level are required for engineering review and compliance sampling.

Success criteria (we'll be strict on these):
- Extraction precision >= 0.86 and recall >= 0.82 on the 200-case seed (we can provide labels by Friday).
- 95p latency < 300ms for single-turn inference and maintain 150-200 qps sustained for batch jobs.
- End-to-end integration with our downstream pipeline (we'll validate JSON schema compatibility).

Questions:
1) What is the expected lead time for VPC onboarding? Do you support cross-account peering or only VPC deployment in our account?
2) Cost posture: can you provide a short estimate for the trial (in terms of reserved compute vs metered)?
3) Do you offer a temporary audit token stream for our SIEM during the trial?

Attached: beta-soc2-questions.xlsx (procurement/security). Procurement copied here for contract/DPA.

We can target provisioning the week of 2025-09-22 as you suggested. Happy to lock a 15m call Monday to go over network details if that helps.

Best,
Alice Maxwell
Product Lead, Beta Health
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Maxwell <alice@beta.health>, Tom Hirsch <tom@beta.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, procurement <procurement@beta.health>
Date: 2025-09-16T13:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Trial hosting posture & initial success criteria

Alice — thanks, and great to see concrete thresholds. Responses inline and a concrete plan: 

Lead time / network model
- We support deployment into customer AWS accounts (cross-account role) or VPC peering depending on networking policy. Typical lead time for VPC onboarding with KMS + audit stream is 3–5 business days once we have the required IAM role and allowlist.

Cost for trial
- For a 2-week VPC trial we usually run a small Dedicated pool sized to target your throughput (we'll size for 200 qps sustained). Estimated trial compute commit is ~$3,500–4,500 (one-off reserved for the trial window) plus token usage metered at standard dev rate. We'll send a short written estimate to procurement.

Audit/logging
- Yes — we can stream token-level audit logs to your SIEM (S3 or Kinesis). Marissa will own delivery on the logging connector.

Proposed plan (updated) — please confirm: 
- 2025-09-18: Procurement — DPA + trial order (procurement@beta.health).
- 2025-09-19 to 2025-09-22: Network prep — provide IAM role, allowlist, KMS key ARN, and sample dataset.
- 2025-09-23 to 2025-09-26: Provisioning & smoke tests (Marissa).
- 2025-09-29 to 2025-10-03: Evaluation window + engineering validation (Alice/Tom).

Action items I own: final estimate to procurement, provide trial MOP (attached), schedule a 15-min network walkthrough Monday 2025-09-22 10:00am PT if that works.

Looping Marissa and Ben to scope the VPC onboarding tasks and capacity sizing.

—Sean
